rows.A_note: Not level 0: EV-171 shows informal individual contact with a university lab with no agreement, which the anchor classes as level 1. EV-170 and EV-171 are consistent on the absence of agreements and publications.
rows.B_note: EV-170 explicitly states absence of all required artefacts, so level 0 is satisfied.

rows.A_note: Mechanism and test coverage for all 14 systems is evidenced by EV-692. Responsibility is evidenced for CTA only, so level 2 fails on that clause. Level 3 would also fail: EV-693 has a metric, a value and a target, but no named reporting body or cadence. If responsibilities for all 14 systems were evidenced, the score would be 2.
rows.B_note: All systems covered, including vendor-dependent; time-to-deactivate measured and reported

rows.A_note: A backlog linked to findings exists (EV-730). Level 3 would also fail: measured effect is recorded for only 7 of 9 releases (EV-732), which is not full coverage. The two-level rule applies, and the level 2 citation coverage is not evidenced for all releases.
rows.B_note: Partial coverage of measured effect per release

rows.A_note: EV-430 and EV-431 show version control and a complete manifest for the 2026-07 run. The audit records a defect for the 3 runs, so level 2 fails. EV-432 also measures reproducibility (9 of 12), which is a level-3 artefact, but it cannot count while level 2 fails.
rows.B_note: All evaluations have manifests, but no measurement of reproducibility share until audit in 2026-09 (EV-432), which is not reported as a metric

rows.A_note: Level 2 is supported by EV-460 (all 14 in-scope systems, with anomaly and drift detection and on-call alerts), although the scope register date is not named. The level-4 threshold change in EV-463 exists, but level 4 is unreachable without the level-3 dated per-system report. EV-463 also cannot be traced to a named motivating report: it is dated 2026-05, before the 2026-08 incident in EV-461.

Level 1 is met because a safety evaluation with fail-safe testing exists (EV-480). The missing acceptance dates and the unverifiable register count are shortfalls under the level-1 anchor. EV-482 confirms there is no re-test, so level 3 tracking is also absent.
rows.B_note: EV-480 and EV-481 satisfy level 2; EV-482 confirms no periodic re-test or tracking

rows.A_note: Level 1 is met by drift monitoring that detected changes (EV-610). EV-613 reports 6 systems with documented change events against 2 declines in EV-610, which is unreconciled. Level 3 would also fail: EV-612 gives medians with no stated target and no named reviewing body.
rows.B_note: EV-612 measures latency and time, but no target or reviewing body
